criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 deletes the prior Customer-ownership language for Customer-Trained Adaptations and replaces it with Vendor ownership plus an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license to Customer covering the fine-tuned adapter weights and related adaptations. This satisfies the required perpetual-license construct.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes Section 5.4, “Non-Assertion Covenant,” under Article 5 (Intellectual Property). It broadly and irrevocably prohibits Vendor and relevant successors, assigns, and acquirers from asserting intellectual property rights against Customer’s permitted post-termination use, deployment, modification, or further development of the exported Customer-Trained Adaptations.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 5.3 requires Vendor, within 30 calendar days after termination or expiration, to provide an API-based export of all current Customer-Trained Adaptations, including adapter weights, in an industry-standard, machine-readable format such as ONNX or SafeTensors. Section 13.6 reinforces the same 30-day API-based export requirement.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly includes escrow as part of the IP protections accompanying the perpetual-license construct. Article 5 links Customer-Trained Adaptations to escrow protections, and Article 5A requires deposit of production fine-tuned adapter weights, training configurations, and necessary pipeline artifacts, with update and release provisions. Sections 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 13.6, and Exhibit E further integrate escrow with portability, non-assertion, and survival rights.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.2 sets the general aggregate liability cap at 1.5× the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly calculated as $3,600,000.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.3 sets a separate super-cap of three times the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly calculated as $7,200,000, and applies it to both Vendor IP indemnification obligations and breaches of Article 6 or Security Breaches involving Customer Data.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.3 expressly excludes liability for willful misconduct and gross negligence from the General Cap and states that such liability remains fully uncapped. The separate 3× super-cap applies only to specified IP indemnification and data-processing/security liabilities, and the text reiterates that no provision caps willful misconduct or gross negligence.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act solely as Customer’s service provider under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and as a processor, prohibits Vendor from acting as an independent controller/business, and includes an explicit CCPA service-provider compliance certification in Exhibit D.

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly prohibits Vendor from using Customer Data, including de-identified or aggregated derivatives, for model improvement unless the data meets the CCPA de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by TechNova verifies the de-identification and provides written certification before use. These requirements are drafted as specific contractual obligations in Section 6.1 and DPA §4.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 9.1 expressly requires Platform availability of at least 99.95% in each calendar month, and Exhibit B and the issues list consistently reflect the same monthly uptime SLA.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 9.1 expressly excludes scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from Downtime for purposes of the 99.95% uptime SLA. It also specifies a four-hour monthly maintenance limit and 72 hours’ advance notice.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly sets the API latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Section 9.2 and conforms Exhibit B to the same threshold.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies the 450 ms latency SLA as a YELLOW/caution item and expressly notes that TechNova’s Product Engineering team prefers sub-400 ms latency.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial F1 threshold at ≥ 0.92 during the Stabilization Period, including in Section 9.3, Exhibit A, and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contractually sets F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period from Go-Live on October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, then increases the required target to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026. This ramp is stated in Section 9.3 and conformed in Exhibits A and B.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly sets the aggregate SLA service credit cap at 20% of monthly fees, equal to $40,000 per month based on the $200,000 monthly platform fee, including in Section 9.4 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 9.5 expressly retains Customer’s right to terminate if Vendor misses any applicable SLA target for three consecutive calendar months. Exhibit B and the issues list also preserve the three-consecutive-month trigger.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 adds Section 11.2, “AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer against third-party claims alleging that AI-generated outputs infringe or violate intellectual property rights or applicable law.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 expressly excludes claims to the extent caused by Customer's modification of an output after receipt or Customer's use of the output outside the documented use case.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 11.1 expressly broadens Vendor’s IP indemnity to cover all intellectual property rights arising from Customer’s authorized use, including patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, publicity rights, moral rights, database rights, and analogous foreign rights. It is not limited to registered U.S. patents and copyrights.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires escrow of production fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts necessary to make the weights usable for the LendStream use case. It expressly excludes Base Model source code and Base Model weights.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the primary Escrow Agent and expressly permits NCC Group plc as a Tier 1 fallback alternative if Iron Mountain cannot be used.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 5A.3 includes all required escrow release triggers: Vendor insolvency, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 calendar days after notice, and cessation, end-of-life, or discontinuation of product support.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 12.1(b) sets Technology E&O / Cyber Liability Insurance at $5,000,000 per occurrence, expressly accepting Meridian's current policy limit.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly flags Tech E&O at $5M as a “YELLOW-ZONE caution” and states that $10M is preferred for TCV exceeding $5M, while noting the platform-fee TCV is at least $7.2M.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly maintains Delaware law in Article 14 and treats Meridian's Massachusetts-law position as open and unaccepted. The issues list also confirms Delaware law remains TechNova's Draft 3 position.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly retains Delaware law and exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, where subject-matter jurisdiction exists, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. It states that the Massachusetts law/Boston AAA arbitration position is not accepted.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes Exhibit D (Data Processing Addendum), whose §1 expressly identifies Vendor as a CCPA “Service Provider” under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and certifies that Vendor will not sell or share Customer Data or retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship or permitted business purposes. The Agreement also reinforces this certification in Section 6.2.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Article 6.3 requires compliance with GLBA implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P and the FTC Safeguards Rule, and DPA §3 requires safeguards consistent with the GLBA Safeguards Rule and Regulation S-P where applicable.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires written breach notification within 72 hours after Vendor first becomes aware of a confirmed or reasonably suspected data breach, including in DPA §5 and Section 6.5.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Customer/TechNova's prior written consent before Vendor may engage, replace, or add any sub-processor that processes Customer Data, both in Section 6.6 and DPA §6.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires de-identified data to satisfy the CCPA statutory standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), including safeguards against re-identification and inadvertent release. It also requires verification by an independent third-party assessor approved by TechNova, with written certification before use. These requirements appear in both Section 6.1 and DPA §4.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses data return and deletion upon termination. Article 13.6 states that Customer Data must be returned or deleted under Article 6 and Exhibit D, and DPA §7 requires Vendor to return or securely delete Customer Data, including copies and backups, within 30 days and certify completion.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/license (5), liability cap (6), data processing/de-identification (8), uptime (1), latency (2), accuracy/F1 (3), SLA credits (4), escrow (13), AI-output indemnity (9), IP indemnity scope (10), Tech E&O insurance (11), and governing law/dispute resolution (12).

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP Ownership / License Structure” as “Partially Resolved,” reflecting that the perpetual-license construct is workable but conditioned on unresolved protections such as portability, non-assertion, and escrow.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the liability cap as “Open,” noting that Draft 3 proposes a 1.5× annual-fee compromise but that no agreement has been reached. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open.”

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 8, “Data Processing / CCPA Service-Provider; de-identified/aggregated data,” is expressly categorized as “Partially Resolved.” The negotiation record states that Meridian agreed to service-provider/DPA terms in principle but has not accepted the proposed independent de-identification certification conditions.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the uptime SLA as “Resolved” and states 99.95% monthly uptime with agreed scheduled-maintenance and Force Majeure exclusions, including 72-hour notice and a four-hour monthly maintenance limit.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the latency SLA as “Partially Resolved,” states that p95 ≤ 450 ms is accepted/proposed as the compromise, and expressly notes that the product team prefers sub-400 ms.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Accuracy / F1 Score (0.92 ramp to 0.94)” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not accepted TechNova’s 0.92 floor.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA Credits (Issue 4) as "Open," reflecting that Draft 3 proposes a 20% compromise that Meridian has not accepted. The criterion expressly permits either "Partially Resolved" or "Open."

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 13, Escrow (scope and agent), as "Open," noting that scope and agent details remain disputed. The criterion expressly permits either "Partially Resolved" or "Open" and only fails a fully "Resolved" classification.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 9, “AI-Output Indemnity,” as “Open” and notes that Meridian’s May 9 response was non-substantive.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP Indemnity Scope (broadening)” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not substantively agreed to the proposed broadening.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Insurance / Tech E&O ($5M accepted)” as “Partially Resolved” and expressly flags it as a “YELLOW-ZONE caution.”

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 12, Governing Law / Dispute Resolution, as “Open” and states there was “no movement,” satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: The document expressly identifies the clean accepted Draft 2 as the base and displays tracked deletions and insertions for Draft 3 changes, including embedded w:del/w:ins revision elements. It is not redlined against Draft 1.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 consistently preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per year, including in the definitions, commercial terms, liability calculations, and issues list.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly preserves a three-year Initial Term from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2028, including in the agreement introduction, Article 13, and the issues list.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the $850,000 implementation fee and expressly splits it 50/50: $425,000 at SOW execution and $425,000 at Go-Live acceptance. This is stated consistently in Article 3, Article 4, Exhibit A, and the updated issues list.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 included API calls per Contract Year and a $0.012 per-call overage rate, including in the definitions, Article 4, and the updated issues list.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly preserves the 180-day auto-renewal/non-renewal notice period in Articles 4 and 13, and the issues list confirms the same commercial term. The notice period was not altered.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list states that p95 ≤450 ms is within the playbook’s acceptable range (≤500 ms) but above the Green/preferred sub-400 ms target. It also notes the Product Engineering preference for sub-400 ms due to potential effects on LendStream real-time decisioning and UX/conversion, satisfying the required context.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The latency issue entry expressly recommends revisiting the p95 ≤450 ms position on the week-of-May-19 joint call, including exploring alternatives such as dedicated compute or regional deployment. This satisfies the requirement to recommend considering latency escalation at that call.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks AI-Output Indemnity as “Open” and expressly states that “Meridian's May 9 response was non-substantive,” accurately reflecting that Meridian had not substantively responded and still needed internal review.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states under Issue 9 (AI-Output Indemnity) that the fallback is a shared-risk framework with Vendor first-dollar coverage if full vendor indemnity is not obtained. This matches the required playbook fallback.
